reason: The text contains multiple named characters who are regular people without special prophetic, judicial, or royal roles. Most prominently, Nabal (נָבָל) is introduced as a wealthy man of Carmel whose character is described through personal and domestic details—his harsh disposition, his wealth in flocks, and his death. Abigail (אֲבִגָיִל), his wife, is similarly portrayed as an ordinary woman, characterized by wisdom and beauty, who acts to prevent disaster through practical intervention. Ahinoam (אֲחִינֹעַם) is another regular person mentioned. While these individuals interact with David (a future king) and thus occupy significant narrative roles, they themselves lack the special status of prophets (like Samuel) or rulers, making them regular people by biblical standards.
